summary: Token refresh retry and the 401 flow

message.content: How do I refresh the token when the API returns 401? It happens on every request after an hour.

content.thinking: The user wants a retry plan. Consider the refresh token lifetime and **rate limits**.

content.text:
## Token refresh plan

The client should **retry once** after a `401`, then *give up*. Steps:

1. Read the refresh token from the keychain
2. Call `POST /oauth/token`
   - with `grant_type=refresh_token`
   - and the client id
3. Retry the original request

> Note: a second 401 means the refresh token itself expired.

| Status | Meaning | Action |
|--------|---------|--------|
| 200 | ok | use the response |
| 401 | expired | refresh, then retry once |
| 429 | rate limited | back off |

```rust
fn refresh(client: &Client) -> Result<Token> {
	let token = client.post("/oauth/token")?;
    Ok(token)
}
```

See [the RFC](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc6749) for details. ~~Old approach~~ is gone.

message.content: Wide table check: show every endpoint with its limits.

content.text:
Here is the full matrix.

| Endpoint | Method | Auth | Rate limit | Retries | Timeout | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| /v1/oauth/token | POST | client secret | 60 per minute per client | once after 401 | 30 s | rotates the refresh token on every call |
| /v1/users/{id} | GET | bearer token | 600 per minute per user | 3 with backoff | 10 s | cached for 5 minutes by the gateway |
| /v1/reports/export | POST | bearer token + admin scope | 5 per hour | never (not idempotent) | 300 s | returns 202 and a job id to poll |

This single paragraph line is deliberately long so that it has to wrap inside the viewer: the TUI clipped such lines at the terminal width (quirk 15), the GUI soft-wraps every text segment instead, keeps the label and timestamp lanes aligned with the first visual row, and only clips collapsed tool output on purpose, where the (N more lines…) row expands it.
